prompt: Given one or more URLs, analyse the available content and produce a Markdown summary that captures:
What the project, tool, library, concept, or article is about.
What problem it solves and why it matters.
How it works and its key technical concepts.
How developers use it in practice.
Its strengths, limitations, trade-offs, and alternatives.
The most useful insights for a software development blog post.
The output should be self-contained enough that another AI agent or writer can use it as context without having to reread every source page.
Instructions
1. Analyse the source
For each URL provided:
Identify the source type: GitHub repository, README, API documentation, technical article, tutorial, specification, or other.
Determine the main purpose and intended audience.
Extract the key ideas, features, design decisions, architecture, workflows, and implementation details.
Identify relevant programming languages, frameworks, libraries, tools, APIs, and dependencies.
Capture important examples, commands, configuration, code snippets, and usage patterns when they help explain the subject.
For GitHub repositories, prioritise the README, project description, installation instructions, usage examples, architecture, dependencies, contribution guidelines, and documented limitations.
Use linked pages or files when they materially improve understanding and are accessible.
Distinguish between what the source explicitly states and what you infer from it.
Do not assume that a repository is actively maintained, production-ready, widely adopted, or secure unless the available evidence supports that conclusion.
2. Produce a structured Markdown summary
Use the following format, omitting sections that are genuinely not applicable.
[Project, Tool, or Topic Name]
Overview
Summarise the subject in 2–4 sentences. Explain what it is, what it does, and why a software developer might care about it.
Problem and Motivation
What problem does it address?
What existing workflow, limitation, or pain point motivates it?
Why might the problem be worth solving?
Key Concepts and Features
List the most important concepts, capabilities, or design principles.
Explain what each one does and why it matters.
Prioritise meaningful functionality over marketing claims.
Technical Details
Languages, frameworks, libraries, and dependencies.
Architecture and major components.
How the system works internally, where documented.
Important APIs, interfaces, configuration options, or data flows.
Relevant implementation details and design decisions.
How It Is Used
Typical developer workflow.
Installation or setup requirements, if relevant.
Important commands, code examples, or configuration patterns.
A concise explanation of how the pieces fit together.
Include code snippets only when they communicate a useful technical concept. Preserve their meaning and do not invent APIs, flags, or functionality.
Never fabricate technical details, source claims, code examples, metrics, citations, or URLs.
Do not treat assumptions, hypotheses, or your own interpretations as documented facts.
You will receive one or more URLs, and optionally a blog BRIEF, and the fetched pge content:
Blog brief:
{BRIEF}
Source URLs:
{URLS}
Fetched page content:
{PAGE_CONTENT}
Return plain text notes under 2500 characters.
Include the most useful facts, examples, and caveats from the fetched pages.
If the pages conflict, note the conflict briefly.
Do not add a preamble.
